name: Multifocal Motor Neuropathy
aliases: Multifocal Motor Neuropathy with Conduction Block

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: EFNS/PNS Diagnostic Criteria for Multifocal Motor Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive, asymmetric distal limb weakness without sensory loss
Motor conduction block on nerve conduction studies in at least one motor nerve
Presence of anti-GM1 IgM antibodies in serum (supportive but not mandatory)
No clinical or electrophysiological evidence of sensory nerve involvement
Clinical improvement with intravenous immunoglobulin therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive asymmetric distal limb weakness without sensory loss plus motor conduction block on nerve conduction studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Anti-GM1 antibodies support diagnosis but are not required; response to IVIG is typical

common.symptomName: Weakness of long finger extensor muscles

laboratory: Elevated anti-GM1 IgM antibodies in serum (in ~50% of cases)
Normal cerebrospinal fluid protein or mildly elevated
imaging: MRI usually normal; may be used to exclude other causes
other: Nerve conduction studies showing motor conduction block without sensory nerve involvement
Positive response to intravenous immunoglobulin therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of upper motor neuron signs
Progressive involvement of both upper and lower motor neurons
No conduction block on nerve conduction studies
Absence of conduction block typical of MMN

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
Lack of response to intravenous immunoglobulin therapy
references: Joint Task Force of the EFNS and the PNS. EFNS/PNS guideline on diagnosis and management of multifocal motor neuropathy. Eur J Neurol. 2010.
Dalakas MC. Multifocal motor neuropathy: an update. Neurology. 2002.
